headline: Highest risk is data leakage from dbt-core’s warehouse access; prompt injection and capability conflict are otherwise limited by the pair’s sparse, docs-only profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-python and dbt-core, and neither profile shows a default path for one agent to ingest the other’s outputs. With only docs-only profiles and no evidence of clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridging, prompt injection is not plausible here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects awesome-python outputs into dbt-core prompts or files, the risk becomes non-none.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe generated text from one agent into the other without sanitization.
Add provenance tags if a shared orchestrator is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, so it can move sensitive warehouse content outward in default use. awesome-python is a docs-only collection with no data-touching surface, so it is not the leakage source; the pair risk is driven by dbt-core’s documented access and egress.
conditions: IF dbt-core is pointed at a warehouse containing sensitive records, leakage risk is present.
IF the allowlist includes external services, warehouse-derived content can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Review the egress allowlist before execution.
Disable any unnecessary adapters or integrations.
Run a dry-run against synthetic data first.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no documented write or network surface, while dbt-core has allowlisted egress and warehouse API access. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, shared filesystem writes, or locking conflicts, so only a small coordination risk remains if an external orchestrator couples them.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same workspace or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state between them, race conditions become plausible.
mitigations: Avoid shared git branches or uncoordinated writes.
Introduce a simple lock if a shared artifact is added.
Run one agent at a time for any future shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where awesome-python produces authoritative facts that dbt-core consumes, and dbt-core is not shown to take autonomous downstream actions like email or commits. Without a verified handoff, cascading error is limited to hypothetical orchestration rather than the pair itself.
conditions: IF awesome-python outputs are later treated as authoritative inputs to dbt-core, the risk becomes medium.
IF dbt-core is configured to act on unverified generated SQL or metadata, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before dbt runs.
Validate any generated SQL against tests.
Log and inspect failed runs before retrying.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which commonly carries regulated or sensitive records, while awesome-python is a non-runnable open-source collection with no data residency or retention controls. The pair creates a compliance gap only through dbt-core’s handling of warehouse data; the other agent is not a compliance driver here.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data, dbt-core processing may trigger residency or retention obligations.
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or retention policy, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Check retention settings for dbt logs and artifacts.
Document the legal basis for any regulated data flow.
